title: no successor in Ensembl's history: a bridge through a shared id
what: a name whose genes Ensembl's history carries to nothing is answered through an external id or a name with a gene that does not overlap the old gene's place
cause: reason:^Ensembl has no successor; not at the query's place

title: a display name asked at its own release is not read there
what: the gene's display cross-reference at the release is filed under a database the graph does not hold at that release (HGNC projections, UniProt entry names, RFAM_gene_name, miRBase_gene_name, WikiGene and RefSeq labels of early releases); the name is read at its latest release (rule `from_release_fallback`) and carried back: lost, or another gene
user_action: ask by the Ensembl id, or without `from_release`
fixed_by: built in idtrack's next version after its first round (tree `r1`): rule `display_names_at_release`

title: a display name held at its own release answers another gene
what: the graph holds the name at the release, and the answer holds a gene Ensembl's display records and name databases do not give it there (miRBase entries the one-gene rule removed or kept: rule `mirbase_genes`; names that other genes carry in a source the truth does not read)
rule: rule `mirbase_genes` (finding AT-3; decided) for miRBase names
user_action: use the `all` view and read the match
fixed_by: partly built after next's first round (tree `r1`): rule `mirbase_genes` by loci; names other databases give other genes: read one by one

title: a display name of the GTF that is an identifier of a database the graph does not hold
what: at mouse release 49 Ensembl's GTF writes the MGI accession (`MGI:2687328`) of 21,182 genes as their name; the graph holds no MGI ids (the package's limitation: identifiers of databases that the graph does not hold answer nothing), so such a name is not found
user_action: ask by the gene's symbol or Ensembl id
fixed_by: none (the package's configuration selects no MGI ids)
